spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m0p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Robots, Total

VARIABLES shelf, transit, snap
vars == <<shelf, transit, snap>>

NoSnap == 0 - 1

Init ==
  /\ shelf = Total
  /\ transit = 0
  /\ snap = [r \in Robots |-> NoSnap]

Snapshot(r) ==
  /\ snap[r] = NoSnap
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = shelf]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, transit>>

Withdraw(r) ==
  /\ snap[r] # NoSnap
  /\ snap[r] = shelf
  /\ shelf > 0
  /\ shelf' = shelf - 1
  /\ transit' = transit + 1
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = NoSnap]

Deposit(r) ==
  /\ snap[r] # NoSnap
  /\ snap[r] = shelf
  /\ transit > 0
  /\ shelf' = shelf + 1
  /\ transit' = transit - 1
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = NoSnap]

Retry(r) ==
  /\ snap[r] # NoSnap
  /\ snap[r] # shelf
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, transit>>

Next == \E r \in Robots : Snapshot(r) \/ Withdraw(r) \/ Deposit(r) \/ Retry(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

QuantityConserved == shelf + transit = Total
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Robots = {r1, r2}
  Total = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT QuantityConserved
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet moves identical parcels between a staging shelf and a set of transit carts. There is a fixed number of parcels in the system that is never manufactured or discarded; each parcel is either resting on the shelf or riding in transit. Two robots operate concurrently and coordinate through optimistic locking: before touching the shelf a robot first takes a snapshot of the shelf's current parcel count, and it may only commit its move if the shelf count still equals that snapshot at commit time. A robot that holds a snapshot may be slow and take arbitrarily long before acting, but it never crashes or vanishes, so its snapshot always remains pending until it acts. If another robot changes the shelf in the meantime, the slow robot's snapshot is stale, and it must abandon the attempt and retry by taking a fresh snapshot. A successful withdraw moves one parcel from the shelf into a transit cart, and a successful deposit returns one parcel from a cart back onto the shelf. Because every committed move relocates exactly one parcel without creating or destroying any, the count on the shelf plus the count in transit stays fixed forever.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of parcels on the shelf plus the number of parcels in transit always equals the fixed total number of parcels in the system.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m2p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cars, Bays

NoBay == "none"
NoCar == "none"

VARIABLES pstate, pending, claim
vars == <<pstate, pending, claim>>

Init ==
  /\ pstate = [b \in Bays |-> "free"]
  /\ pending = [b \in Bays |-> NoCar]
  /\ claim = [c \in Cars |-> NoBay]

Prepare(b, c) ==
  /\ pstate[b] = "free"
  /\ claim[c] = NoBay
  /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![b] = "prepared"]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED claim

Commit(b) ==
  /\ pstate[b] = "prepared"
  /\ pending[b] # NoCar
  /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![b] = "committed"]
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![pending[b]] = b]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![b] = NoCar]

Abort(b) ==
  /\ pstate[b] = "prepared"
  /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![b] = NoCar]
  /\ UNCHANGED claim

Release(b, c) ==
  /\ pstate[b] = "committed"
  /\ claim[c] = b
  /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoBay]
  /\ UNCHANGED pending

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bays, c \in Cars : Prepare(b, c)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : Commit(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : Abort(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays, c \in Cars : Release(b, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A c1 \in Cars : \A c2 \in Cars :
    (claim[c1] # NoBay /\ claim[c1] = claim[c2]) => c1 = c2
====
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line assigns wash bays to arriving cars using a two-phase commit protocol run by a line coordinator across the bay's participant stations (soaker, scrubber, dryer). Each bay is free, prepared, or committed. To claim a free bay for a car that does not already hold a bay, the coordinator first moves the bay into the prepared phase and records that car as the pending claimant; this is the voting phase in which the stations are asked to reserve. If every station is ready, the coordinator commits: the bay becomes committed and the car's local claim record is set to that bay. Any station may crash silently and simply fail to acknowledge, in which case the coordinator aborts the prepared bay, releasing it back to free and dropping the pending claimant, so a crash never leaves a bay half-assigned. When a car finishes its wash it releases its committed bay, clearing its claim record and returning the bay to free for reuse. Because a bay can enter the prepared phase only while it is free, and only the single pending claimant is ever committed onto it, no two cars ever end up holding a claim to the same bay.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct cars simultaneously hold a claim record pointing to the same wash bay.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m8p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Workers, MinCap, MaxCap

None == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, done, cap
vars == <<coarse, fine, done, cap>>

Init ==
  /\ coarse = None
  /\ fine = None
  /\ done = {}
  /\ cap = MaxCap

AcquireCoarse(w) ==
  /\ coarse = None
  /\ coarse' = w
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, done, cap>>

AcquireFine(w) ==
  /\ coarse = w
  /\ fine = None
  /\ fine' = w
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, done, cap>>

Apply(w) ==
  /\ coarse = w
  /\ fine = w
  /\ w \notin done
  /\ Cardinality(done) < cap
  /\ done' = done \cup {w}
  /\ coarse' = None
  /\ fine' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED cap

Reconfigure ==
  /\ \E k \in MinCap..MaxCap : k >= Cardinality(done) /\ cap' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, done>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Workers : AcquireCoarse(w) \/ AcquireFine(w) \/ Apply(w)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
  /\ (fine # None => coarse = fine)
  /\ Cardinality(done) <= cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  MinCap = 1
  MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps a shared manifest record that worker processes update as bags are scanned. To prevent lost updates the router uses hierarchical locking: a worker must first acquire the coarse lock covering the whole manifest, then acquire the single fine write-lock, and only while holding both may it commit its scan into the manifest. A worker holds the coarse lock exclusively, then descends to take the fine lock, applies its update by adding its token to the manifest, and releases both locks in one step. The manifest has a runtime-adjustable capacity: an operator may reconfigure the maximum number of committed scans up or down at any time, but never below the number already committed. Because the fine write-lock can only ever be held by a worker that also holds the coarse lock, two workers can never both be inside the write section at once, so no committed update is ever overwritten or lost. The reconfiguration action only changes the capacity bound and never touches the committed manifest entries.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No worker ever holds the fine write-lock without also holding the coarse manifest lock, and the number of committed manifest entries never exceeds the current capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m9p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS MaxEpoch, MaxCap

NoTicket == 0 - 1

VARIABLES epoch, capacity, onLine, ticket
vars == <<epoch, capacity, onLine, ticket>>

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ capacity = 2
  /\ onLine = 0
  /\ ticket = NoTicket

IssueTicket ==
  /\ ticket = NoTicket
  /\ ticket' = epoch
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, onLine>>

Board ==
  /\ ticket = epoch
  /\ onLine < capacity
  /\ onLine' = onLine + 1
  /\ ticket' = NoTicket
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>

DiscardStale ==
  /\ ticket # NoTicket
  /\ ticket # epoch
  /\ ticket' = NoTicket
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, onLine>>

Crash ==
  /\ ticket # NoTicket
  /\ ticket' = NoTicket
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, onLine>>

Exit ==
  /\ onLine > 0
  /\ onLine' = onLine - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, ticket>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ \E k \in 1..MaxCap : k >= onLine /\ capacity' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, ticket>>

Next == IssueTicket \/ Board \/ DiscardStale \/ Crash \/ Exit \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityNeverExceeded == onLine <= capacity
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  MaxEpoch = 2
  MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line admits cars onto a moving belt whose capacity can be reconfigured while running. Reconfiguration is epoch-numbered: each time an operator changes the belt capacity the epoch counter is bumped, and the operator may only choose a new capacity that is at least the number of cars already on the belt. A car that wants to board first takes an admission ticket stamped with the current epoch. It may drive onto the belt only if its ticket still carries the current epoch and the belt is below capacity; boarding consumes the ticket and adds one car to the belt. If a reconfiguration happens after a car took its ticket, that ticket becomes stale and is discarded before the car can board, forcing it to take a fresh ticket. A waiting car may also crash silently: it simply abandons its ticket and disappears, which the line does not detect and which frees the ticket for reissue. Cars already on the belt eventually exit, decreasing the count. Because a car boards only while the belt is strictly below the current capacity, and every reconfiguration keeps capacity at or above the current load, the number of cars on the belt never exceeds the current capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars on the conveyor belt never exceeds the current reconfigured capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m8p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Patrons, Books

None == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, issuedTo, inbox
vars == <<coarse, fine, issuedTo, inbox>>

Msgs == [patron : Patrons, book : Books]

Init ==
  /\ coarse = None
  /\ fine = [b \in Books |-> None]
  /\ issuedTo = [b \in Books |-> None]
  /\ inbox = {}

Request(p, b) ==
  /\ [patron |-> p, book |-> b] \notin inbox
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[patron |-> p, book |-> b]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, issuedTo>>

AcquireShelf(p) ==
  /\ coarse = None
  /\ coarse' = p
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, issuedTo, inbox>>

AcquireBook(p, b) ==
  /\ coarse = p
  /\ fine[b] = None
  /\ issuedTo[b] = None
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, issuedTo, inbox>>

Issue(p, b) ==
  /\ coarse = p
  /\ fine[b] = p
  /\ issuedTo[b] = None
  /\ [patron |-> p, book |-> b] \in inbox
  /\ issuedTo' = [issuedTo EXCEPT ![b] = p]
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = None]
  /\ coarse' = None
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {[patron |-> p, book |-> b]}

ReleaseBook(p, b) ==
  /\ fine[b] = p
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, issuedTo, inbox>>

ReleaseShelf(p) ==
  /\ coarse = p
  /\ \A b \in Books : fine[b] # p
  /\ coarse' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, issuedTo, inbox>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : Request(p, b) \/ AcquireBook(p, b) \/ Issue(p, b) \/ ReleaseBook(p, b)
  \/ \E p \in Patrons : AcquireShelf(p) \/ ReleaseShelf(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOnceIssue ==
  \A b \in Books :
    /\ (issuedTo[b] # None => fine[b] = None)
    /\ (fine[b] # None => coarse = fine[b])
====
nl:
A library book reservation system fulfills patron reservations by issuing a physical copy to exactly one patron. Reservation requests travel over a network that may reorder them, so pending requests are held in an unordered inbox and may be processed in any order. Issuing a book is irreversible: once a copy has been handed to a patron it is never taken back or re-issued. To issue safely the clerk uses hierarchical locking: it first acquires the coarse shelf lock, then the fine per-book lock, and a book may only be fine-locked when it is not already issued. While holding the shelf lock and that book's fine lock, and with a matching request in the inbox, the clerk issues the book to the requesting patron, records the issuance, consumes the request, and releases both locks. A clerk that cannot find a matching request may simply release the book's fine lock and later the shelf lock without issuing. Because a book can be fine-locked for issuing only while it is not yet issued, an already-issued book can never be locked again, so no copy is ever issued a second time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a book has been issued to a patron it is never again placed under a fine lock, so it can never be issued more than once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m3p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes

None == "none"

VARIABLES leader, up, inCSleader, inCSadmin
vars == <<leader, up, inCSleader, inCSadmin>>

Init ==
  /\ leader = None
  /\ up = Nodes
  /\ inCSleader = FALSE
  /\ inCSadmin = FALSE

Elect(n) ==
  /\ leader = None
  /\ n \in up
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, inCSleader, inCSadmin>>

Fail(n) ==
  /\ n \in up
  /\ up' = up \ {n}
  /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN None ELSE leader
  /\ inCSleader' = IF leader = n THEN FALSE ELSE inCSleader
  /\ UNCHANGED inCSadmin

LeaderEnter(n) ==
  /\ leader = n
  /\ ~inCSadmin
  /\ ~inCSleader
  /\ inCSleader' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, inCSadmin>>

LeaderExit ==
  /\ inCSleader
  /\ inCSleader' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, inCSadmin>>

AdminForceRelease ==
  /\ inCSleader
  /\ inCSleader' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, inCSadmin>>

AdminEnter ==
  /\ ~inCSleader
  /\ ~inCSadmin
  /\ inCSadmin' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, inCSleader>>

AdminExit ==
  /\ inCSadmin
  /\ inCSadmin' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, inCSleader>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n) \/ Fail(n) \/ LeaderEnter(n)
  \/ LeaderExit \/ AdminForceRelease \/ AdminEnter \/ AdminExit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualExclusion == ~(inCSleader /\ inCSadmin)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A university course-registration system lets several server nodes contend for exclusive write access to the registration ledger, coordinated by leader election with failover. At most one node is the elected leader at a time; a node may become leader only when there is no current leader and the node is still alive. Only the current leader may enter the critical section that writes the ledger, and it may do so only when the section is free. Any leader may crash and fail silently, which removes it from the alive set, clears the leadership, and frees the critical section so a new leader can be elected. There is a privileged admin override: the administrator does not need to win the election and can force the current leader out of the critical section, then take exclusive access directly. The admin may enter the section only when the leader is not inside it, and releases it when done. Because a node enters only when the admin is absent and the admin enters only when no leader is inside, the leader and the admin are never in the critical section at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The elected leader and the admin are never inside the ledger critical section simultaneously.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m9p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Devices, MaxEpoch

None == "none"

VARIABLES epoch, grantee, synced, holder
vars == <<epoch, grantee, synced, holder>>

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ grantee \in Devices
  /\ synced = [d \in Devices |-> 0]
  /\ holder = None

Reconfigure ==
  /\ holder = None
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ grantee' \in Devices
  /\ UNCHANGED <<synced, holder>>

Sync(d) ==
  /\ synced[d] < epoch
  /\ synced' = [synced EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee, holder>>

Open(d) ==
  /\ holder = None
  /\ grantee = d
  /\ synced[d] = epoch
  /\ holder' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee, synced>>

Close(d) ==
  /\ holder = d
  /\ holder' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee, synced>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E d \in Devices : Sync(d) \/ Open(d) \/ Close(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DoorMutualExclusion ==
  holder # None => (grantee = holder /\ synced[holder] = epoch)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Devices = {d1, d2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DoorMutualExclusion
nl:
A smart-home door lock network coordinates several devices that may open a single shared door, which is the critical resource. Access rights are managed by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a hub keeps an epoch counter, and each reconfiguration bumps the epoch and grants opening rights to exactly one chosen device, but only while the door is closed. A device learns of a new epoch by syncing: it may be slow to sync and lag behind the current epoch, but it never crashes, so it can always eventually catch up. A device may open the door only when the door is closed, the device is the current grantee, and the device has synced to the current epoch; a slow device that has not yet synced simply cannot open. The device that opened the door later closes it. Because only the current synced grantee can ever open the door and the door holds at most one opener, two devices never have the door open at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the door is open, its opener is the current epoch's sole grantee and has synced to the current epoch, so no two devices open the door at once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m8p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Robots, Pallets

None == "none"

VARIABLES dock, palletLock, dispatched, alive
vars == <<dock, palletLock, dispatched, alive>>

Init ==
  /\ dock = None
  /\ palletLock = [p \in Pallets |-> None]
  /\ dispatched = [p \in Pallets |-> FALSE]
  /\ alive = Robots

AcquireDock(r) ==
  /\ r \in alive
  /\ dock = None
  /\ dock' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<palletLock, dispatched, alive>>

AcquirePallet(r, p) ==
  /\ dock = r
  /\ palletLock[p] = None
  /\ ~dispatched[p]
  /\ palletLock' = [palletLock EXCEPT ![p] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, dispatched, alive>>

Dispatch(r, p) ==
  /\ dock = r
  /\ palletLock[p] = r
  /\ ~dispatched[p]
  /\ dispatched' = [dispatched EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ palletLock' = [palletLock EXCEPT ![p] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, alive>>

ReleasePallet(r, p) ==
  /\ palletLock[p] = r
  /\ palletLock' = [palletLock EXCEPT ![p] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, dispatched, alive>>

ReleaseDock(r) ==
  /\ dock = r
  /\ \A p \in Pallets : palletLock[p] # r
  /\ dock' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<palletLock, dispatched, alive>>

Crash(r) ==
  /\ r \in alive
  /\ alive' = alive \ {r}
  /\ dock' = IF dock = r THEN None ELSE dock
  /\ palletLock' = [p \in Pallets |-> IF palletLock[p] = r THEN None ELSE palletLock[p]]
  /\ UNCHANGED dispatched

Recover(r) ==
  /\ r \notin alive
  /\ alive' = alive \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, palletLock, dispatched>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots : AcquireDock(r) \/ ReleaseDock(r) \/ Crash(r) \/ Recover(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, p \in Pallets : AcquirePallet(r, p) \/ Dispatch(r, p) \/ ReleasePallet(r, p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOnceDispatch ==
  /\ \A p \in Pallets : dispatched[p] => palletLock[p] = None
  /\ \A p \in Pallets : palletLock[p] # None => palletLock[p] = dock
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet loads pallets onto an outbound truck. Dispatching a pallet onto the truck is irreversible: once dispatched it is gone and can never be dispatched again. Robots coordinate with hierarchical locking: a robot must first take the coarse dock lock, then take the fine per-pallet lock, and a pallet may be fine-locked only if it has not already been dispatched. While holding the dock lock and a pallet's fine lock, a robot dispatches that pallet, marks it dispatched, and releases that pallet's fine lock while keeping the dock lock so it can dispatch further pallets; it releases the dock lock separately once it holds no pallet locks. A robot may crash silently at any time: it vanishes from the alive set and all locks it was holding, coarse and fine, are released so the fleet is not stranded. A crashed robot may later be power-cycled and rejoin the fleet. A robot that decides not to dispatch may simply release the pallet lock and then the dock lock. Because a pallet can be fine-locked for dispatch only while it is undispatched, a dispatched pallet is never locked again and so is never dispatched twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A pallet that has been dispatched is never again held under a fine lock, so no pallet is dispatched more than once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m7p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Elevators

Free == "free"
Admin == "admin"
Recalled == "recalled"
NoTrigger == "none"

VARIABLES reg, recalledBy
vars == <<reg, recalledBy>>

Init ==
  /\ reg = Free
  /\ recalledBy = NoTrigger

Claim(e) ==
  /\ reg = Free
  /\ reg' = e
  /\ UNCHANGED recalledBy

Release(e) ==
  /\ reg = e
  /\ reg' = Free
  /\ UNCHANGED recalledBy

Recall(e) ==
  /\ reg = e
  /\ reg' = Recalled
  /\ recalledBy' = e

AdminSeize ==
  /\ reg # Recalled
  /\ reg' = Admin
  /\ UNCHANGED recalledBy

AdminRecall ==
  /\ reg = Admin
  /\ reg' = Recalled
  /\ recalledBy' = Admin

Idle ==
  /\ reg = Recalled
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E e \in Elevators : Claim(e) \/ Release(e) \/ Recall(e)
  \/ AdminSeize \/ AdminRecall \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RecallAtMostOnce == (reg = Recalled) <=> (recalledBy # NoTrigger)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Elevators = {e1, e2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RecallAtMostOnce
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper coordinates its cars through a single shared compare-and-swap control register. The register is either free, owned by one elevator, owned by the admin, or latched to the recalled state. An elevator acquires control by a compare-and-swap that succeeds only when the register is free, swapping it to that elevator's identity; the elevator may later release it back to free. The irreversible action is an emergency recall: the elevator (or the admin) that currently owns the register drives all cars to the ground and latches the register to the recalled state, recording who triggered it. Recall is irreversible and happens at most once: once the register is latched to recalled, no compare-and-swap, release, or further recall can ever change it again, and the recalled shaft simply idles in that latched state. There is a privileged admin override: the administrator can seize the register directly whenever it is not already recalled, bypassing the compare-and-swap, and may then trigger the recall itself. Because the register can only ever move into the recalled state while it has an owner, and can never leave it, the recorded trigger is set exactly when the register is recalled.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The control register is in the recalled state if and only if a recall trigger has been recorded, and once recalled it never changes, so the recall happens at most once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m7p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Drones, MaxVer

None == "none"

VARIABLES regVer, owner, cached, inbox
vars == <<regVer, owner, cached, inbox>>

Init ==
  /\ regVer = 0
  /\ owner = None
  /\ cached = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ inbox = {}

SendCmd(d) ==
  /\ d \notin inbox
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, owner, cached>>

Sync(d) ==
  /\ cached[d] < regVer
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![d] = regVer]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, owner, inbox>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ regVer < MaxVer
  /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
  /\ owner' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cached, inbox>>

Acquire(d) ==
  /\ owner = None
  /\ cached[d] = regVer
  /\ owner' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, cached, inbox>>

Act(d) ==
  /\ owner = d
  /\ cached[d] = regVer
  /\ d \in inbox
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {d}
  /\ owner' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, cached>>

Release(d) ==
  /\ owner = d
  /\ owner' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, cached, inbox>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E d \in Drones : SendCmd(d) \/ Sync(d) \/ Acquire(d) \/ Act(d) \/ Release(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleHolder == owner # None => cached[owner] = regVer
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Drones = {a1, a2}
  MaxVer = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleHolder
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a single command register that decides which drone may execute the next surveillance sweep. The register carries a version number that the ground station advances whenever it reconfigures the mission; advancing the version also revokes any current ownership of the register. Each drone caches the version number it last learned, and it may sync to refresh its cache up to the current version, but because control messages travel over a lossy radio mesh that can reorder them, a drone's cache may lag behind. A drone is considered current (authorized) only when its cached version equals the register's version; a drone whose cache is stale is unauthorized. To take a turn a drone performs a compare-and-swap that succeeds only when the register is unowned and the drone is current, making it the owner. Pending sweep commands sit in an unordered mailbox and may be handled in any order; the owner executes a queued command only while still current, then releases the register. Because ownership is granted only to a current drone and every version advance clears ownership, the register is never held by a stale or unauthorized drone.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the command register is owned, its owner's cached version equals the register's current version, so no stale or unauthorized drone ever holds it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m7p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Workers, MaxTicket

None == "none"
AdminId == "admin"

VARIABLES reg, holder, myTicket, authorized
vars == <<reg, holder, myTicket, authorized>>

Init ==
  /\ reg = 0
  /\ holder = None
  /\ myTicket = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ authorized = {}

Grant(w) ==
  /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, holder, myTicket>>

Revoke(w) ==
  /\ authorized' = authorized \ {w}
  /\ holder' = IF holder = w THEN None ELSE holder
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, myTicket>>

Sync(w) ==
  /\ myTicket[w] # reg
  /\ myTicket' = [myTicket EXCEPT ![w] = reg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, holder, authorized>>

Acquire(w) ==
  /\ holder = None
  /\ w \in authorized
  /\ myTicket[w] = reg
  /\ holder' = w
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, myTicket, authorized>>

Spool(w) ==
  /\ holder = w
  /\ myTicket[w] = reg
  /\ reg < MaxTicket
  /\ reg' = reg + 1
  /\ holder' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<myTicket, authorized>>

AdminSeize ==
  /\ holder # AdminId
  /\ holder' = AdminId
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, myTicket, authorized>>

AdminRelease ==
  /\ holder = AdminId
  /\ holder' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, myTicket, authorized>>

Next ==
  \/ AdminSeize \/ AdminRelease
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Grant(w) \/ Revoke(w) \/ Sync(w) \/ Acquire(w) \/ Spool(w)

NoUnauthorizedOrStaleHolder ==
  holder # None =>
    \/ holder = AdminId
    \/ (holder \in authorized /\ myTicket[holder] = reg)
====

CONSTANTS
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  MaxTicket = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedOrStaleHolder
nl:
A print shop job spooler serializes access to a shared print queue using a compare-and-swap ticket register. The register holds a ticket number that advances by one every time a job is spooled. Each worker caches the ticket it last observed and may sync to refresh it to the current register value. A worker is authorized only if the shop supervisor has placed it in the authorized set. To take a turn a worker performs a compare-and-swap that succeeds only when the register is unowned, the worker is authorized, and the worker's cached ticket equals the current register value; it then becomes the register's holder. The holder spools one job, advancing the register ticket, which leaves its own cache stale and releases the register. There is a privileged admin override: the supervisor may seize the register directly at any time regardless of ownership, and may later release it. The supervisor may also revoke a worker's authorization, and if that worker currently holds the register its ownership is dropped. Because ownership is only granted to an authorized worker whose cached ticket is current, and revocation or ticket advancement immediately clears a now-stale or unauthorized holder, the register is never held by a stale or unauthorized worker.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the ticket register is held by a worker, that worker is authorized and its cached ticket equals the current register value, so no stale or unauthorized worker ever holds it.

CONSTANTS
  Orders = {o1, o2, o3}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A stock exchange opening auction accepts order submissions into a bounded intake queue that feeds a matching engine which maintains a shared order-book record. The intake queue applies backpressure: a new order can be enqueued only when it is not already pending or applied and the queue is below its capacity bound, so submissions are refused once the queue is full. The matching engine takes one pending order at a time, applies it to the shared order book by recording the order as applied and incrementing the book's running count, so each order contributes exactly one increment and no update is lost. There is a privileged admin override: an exchange administrator may inject an order directly into the queue even when it is at capacity, bypassing backpressure, and may also flush the entire pending queue at any time. Flushing only discards not-yet-applied pending orders and never touches the order book, and injection likewise only adds a pending order. Because the running book count is advanced exactly once per applied order and applied orders are recorded in the applied set, the book count always equals the number of applied orders.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared order book's running count always equals the number of orders recorded as applied, so no applied update is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od8m9p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Students, MaxEpoch, InitialSeats

NoTicket == 0 - 1

VARIABLES epoch, enrolled, seats, ticket
vars == <<epoch, enrolled, seats, ticket>>

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ enrolled = [s \in Students |-> FALSE]
  /\ seats = InitialSeats
  /\ ticket = [s \in Students |-> NoTicket]

Register(s) ==
  /\ ticket[s] = NoTicket
  /\ ~enrolled[s]
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, enrolled, seats>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, seats, ticket>>

Finalize(s) ==
  /\ ticket[s] = epoch
  /\ ~enrolled[s]
  /\ seats > 0
  /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ seats' = seats - 1
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoTicket]
  /\ UNCHANGED epoch

DiscardStale(s) ==
  /\ ticket[s] # NoTicket
  /\ ticket[s] # epoch
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoTicket]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, enrolled, seats>>

AdminOverride(s) ==
  /\ ~enrolled[s]
  /\ seats > 0
  /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ seats' = seats - 1
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoTicket]
  /\ UNCHANGED epoch

ClosedIdle ==
  /\ \A s \in Students : enrolled[s]
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure \/ ClosedIdle
  \/ \E s \in Students : Register(s) \/ Finalize(s) \/ DiscardStale(s) \/ AdminOverride(s)

EnrollmentConserved ==
  seats = InitialSeats - Cardinality({s \in Students : enrolled[s]})
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Students = {s1, s2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
  InitialSeats = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT EnrollmentConserved
nl:
A university course-registration system finalizes student enrollments against a fixed pool of seats. Finalizing an enrollment is irreversible and consumes exactly one seat, and it may happen at most once per student. Registration runs under epoch-numbered reconfiguration: an epoch counter is bumped each time the registrar reconfigures the round, and a student first submits a request stamped with the current epoch. A student's enrollment is finalized only when the student is not already enrolled, the student's request still carries the current epoch, and at least one seat remains; finalizing marks the student enrolled, decrements the seat pool, and clears the request. If a reconfiguration bumps the epoch after a request was stamped, that request is stale and is discarded, so the student must resubmit. There is a privileged admin override: the registrar may force-enroll a not-yet-enrolled student directly, bypassing the epoch check, still consuming one seat. Once every student is enrolled the system idles. Because both the normal and override finalize paths require the student to be currently unenrolled and each decrements the seat pool exactly once, the remaining seats always equal the initial pool minus the number of enrolled students.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of remaining seats always equals the initial seat pool minus the number of students whose enrollment has been finalized, so no student is finalized more than once.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks

None == "none"

VARIABLES blockOwner, pos, alive
vars == <<blockOwner, pos, alive>>

Init ==
  /\ blockOwner = [b \in Blocks |-> None]
  /\ pos = [t \in Trains |-> None]
  /\ alive = Trains

Enter(t, b) ==
  /\ t \in alive
  /\ pos[t] = None
  /\ blockOwner[b] = None
  /\ blockOwner' = [blockOwner EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED alive

Leave(t) ==
  /\ pos[t] # None
  /\ t \in alive
  /\ blockOwner' = [blockOwner EXCEPT ![pos[t]] = None]
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED alive

Crash(t) ==
  /\ t \in alive
  /\ alive' = alive \ {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockOwner, pos>>

Recover(t) ==
  /\ t \notin alive
  /\ alive' = alive \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockOwner, pos>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Enter(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Leave(t) \/ Crash(t) \/ Recover(t)

OneTrainPerBlock ==
  \A t \in Trains : pos[t] # None => blockOwner[pos[t]] = t
====
nl:
A subway signalling block system divides the track into fixed blocks, each of which is a critical resource that at most one train may occupy. Each block has a compare-and-swap ownership register that is either free or held by one train. A train that is not currently in any block may enter a free block by a compare-and-swap that succeeds only when the block's register is free, atomically claiming the register and moving the train into that block. A train leaves its block by releasing the register and clearing its position. A train may crash silently at any time: it drops out of the alive set but, because the crash is undetected, it keeps its position and its block register stays held, so no other train can enter that block. A crashed train may later be recovered and rejoin the alive set. Because a train records itself as a block's owner exactly when it enters, and a block's register can hold only one owner, whenever a train is in a block that block's register names that train.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a train occupies a block, that block's ownership register names exactly that train, so no two trains ever occupy the same block.

---- MODULE W4Od16m4p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS CapQ, CapB

VARIABLES qlen, bays, crashed
vars == <<qlen, bays, crashed>>

  /\ qlen = 0
  /\ bays = 0
  /\ crashed = 0

Arrive ==
  /\ qlen < CapQ
  /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bays, crashed>>

StartDispense ==
  /\ qlen > 0
  /\ bays < CapB
  /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
  /\ bays' = bays + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

FinishDispense ==
  /\ bays > crashed
  /\ bays' = bays - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, crashed>>

Crash ==
  /\ bays > crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, bays>>

ClearCrashed ==
  /\ crashed > 0
  /\ crashed' = crashed - 1
  /\ bays' = bays - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED qlen

Next == Arrive \/ StartDispense \/ FinishDispense \/ Crash \/ ClearCrashed

  /\ qlen <= CapQ
  /\ bays <= CapB
  /\ crashed <= bays
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  CapQ = 2
  CapB = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser has a bounded intake queue feeding a bounded set of dispensing bays. Incoming prescriptions join the intake queue, but the queue applies backpressure: a prescription can be admitted only while the queue is below its capacity, so arrivals are refused when it is full. A worker starts dispensing by pulling one prescription from the queue into a free bay, but only while the number of occupied bays is below the bay capacity. A worker finishing a dispense frees its bay. A worker may crash silently while dispensing: its bay stays occupied and stuck, and the running protocol does not detect the crash, so that bay never completes on its own. A periodic maintenance audit eventually clears a stuck crashed bay, freeing it. Because prescriptions are admitted only while the queue is below its capacity and bays are occupied only while below the bay capacity, neither the queue length nor the number of occupied bays ever exceeds its bound, and stuck bays are always a subset of occupied bays.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The intake queue length never exceeds the queue capacity and the number of occupied dispensing bays never exceeds the bay capacity.

  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A stock exchange opening auction runs two independent matching instances that draw liquidity from one shared pool of share-units. The total number of share-units in the system is fixed and is never created or destroyed; at any moment each unit is either sitting in the shared pool or checked out to instance A or instance B. Either instance may allocate a unit by taking one from the pool into its own holding, and may return a unit by moving one of its holdings back to the pool. Allocation is possible only while the pool is non-empty, and return only while the instance holds at least one unit. The auction reconfigures under an epoch counter: each reconfiguration bumps the epoch and reallocates by draining both instances' holdings entirely back into the shared pool, which redistributes liquidity without minting or destroying any units. Because every allocate, return, and reconfiguration action only relocates units among the pool and the two instances, the total across the pool and both instances stays constant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of units in the shared pool plus the units held by instance A plus the units held by instance B always equals the fixed system total.

CONSTANTS
  N = 2
  Slots = {sa, sb}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A smart-home door lock network shares a set of access time-slots among its devices, coordinated by a token ring. Exactly one device holds the circulating token at any time, and only the token holder may allocate a slot. Devices send allocation requests over a mesh that may reorder them, so pending requests sit in an unordered request set and can be served in any order. When the token holder has a pending request for a slot that is currently unowned in the authoritative slot table, it allocates that slot by writing itself as the slot's owner, incrementing a global counter of granted allocations, and clearing that request. The token holder passes the token to another device around the ring whether or not it allocated anything. Because a slot can be allocated only while it is unowned, each slot transitions from unowned to owned exactly once, so the count of granted allocations always equals the number of slots that currently have an owner. If a slot were ever allocated twice, the granted counter would advance while the number of owned slots stayed the same, so equality of the two would be broken.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The running count of granted allocations always equals the number of slots that currently have an owner, so no slot is ever allocated more than once.

---- MODULE W4Od13m2p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cap

VARIABLES phase, stock, voteM, voteW
vars == <<phase, stock, voteM, voteW>>

Init ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ stock = 0
  /\ voteM = "pending"
  /\ voteW = "pending"

Propose ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ phase' = "voting"
  /\ voteM' = "pending"
  /\ voteW' = "pending"
  /\ UNCHANGED stock

MachineVote ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ voteM = "pending"
  /\ voteM' = IF stock < Cap THEN "yes" ELSE "no"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, stock, voteW>>

WarehouseVote ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ voteW = "pending"
  /\ voteW' \in {"yes", "no"}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, stock, voteM>>

Commit ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ voteM = "yes"
  /\ voteW = "yes"
  /\ stock' = stock + 1
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<voteM, voteW>>

  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ (voteM = "no" \/ voteW = "no")
  /\ phase' = "idle"

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedStock
nl:
A vending machine network restocks a machine through a two-phase commit run by a coordinator across two participants: the machine controller and the warehouse. The machine has a fixed shelf capacity that its stock must never exceed. A restock transaction proceeds in phases: while idle the coordinator opens a voting round; the machine controller votes yes only if the current stock is below capacity, otherwise no; and the warehouse votes yes only if it has a unit to give, otherwise no. Either participant may be slow and cast its vote after an arbitrary delay, but neither ever fails, so both votes are eventually cast. The coordinator commits, adding exactly one unit to the machine, only when both participants have voted yes; if either votes no the round is aborted and the machine returns to idle without changing stock. Independently, the machine may sell a unit whenever its stock is positive, decreasing the stock. Because a unit is added only after the machine controller has confirmed there is room and no other action increases the stock during a voting round, the machine's stock never exceeds its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The machine's stock level never exceeds its fixed shelf capacity.

  /\ fine' = None

  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, book, applied>>

NoLostUpdate == book = Cardinality(applied)

CONSTANTS

nl:
A stock exchange opening auction aggregates matched trades into a shared order-book record, maintained as a running count of committed contributions. Worker processes commit their contributions under hierarchical locking: a worker must first acquire the coarse book lock, then the fine write-lock, and only while holding both may it commit. Committing records the worker in the applied set and increments the book's running count by exactly one, then releases both locks. Each worker contributes at most once, since committing requires the worker not to be already in the applied set. A worker may crash silently while holding locks: it simply drops both the coarse and fine locks without committing, and the shared record is left untouched, so its absent contribution costs nothing and no committed update is lost. Workers that decide not to commit may also release their locks explicitly. Because the running count is advanced exactly once for each worker added to the applied set, and crashes never alter the record, the book count always equals the number of workers in the applied set.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The order book's running count always equals the number of workers recorded in the applied set, so no committed update is ever lost.

CONSTANTS
  Patrons = {p1, p2}
  Total = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CopiesConserved
nl:
A library book reservation system manages a fixed collection of identical copies that are always either on the shelf or loaned out; the total number of copies is fixed and copies are never created or destroyed. Patrons submit borrow and return requests over a network that may reorder them, so pending requests sit in an unordered inbox and may be processed in any order. Access to move a copy is serialized by a single compare-and-swap register: a patron acquires the register by a compare-and-swap that succeeds only when it is free, becoming its holder. While holding the register and with a matching borrow request pending, the holder moves one copy from the shelf to the loaned pile, provided the shelf is non-empty; while holding it with a matching return request pending, the holder moves one copy from the loaned pile back to the shelf, provided the loaned pile is non-empty. Each such move consumes the matching request and releases the register. A holder with no matching request may simply release the register. Because every move relocates exactly one copy between the shelf and the loaned pile without adding or removing any, the number on the shelf plus the number loaned stays equal to the fixed total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of copies on the shelf plus the number of copies loaned out always equals the fixed total number of copies.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m3p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, Cap

None == "none"

VARIABLES leader, up, onBelt
vars == <<leader, up, onBelt>>

Init ==
  /\ leader = None
  /\ up = Nodes
  /\ onBelt = 0

Elect(n) ==
  /\ leader = None
  /\ n \in up
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, onBelt>>

Admit(n) ==
  /\ leader = n
  /\ onBelt < Cap
  /\ onBelt' = onBelt + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up>>

Exit ==
  /\ onBelt > 0
  /\ onBelt' = onBelt - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up>>

Crash(n) ==
  /\ n \in up
  /\ up' = up \ {n}
  /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN None ELSE leader
  /\ UNCHANGED onBelt

Recover(n) ==
  /\ n \notin up
  /\ up' = up \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, onBelt>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n) \/ Admit(n) \/ Crash(n) \/ Recover(n)
  \/ Exit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BoundedBelt == onBelt <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedBelt
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line admits cars onto a belt of bounded capacity, and admissions are controlled by a single elected leader among the control nodes with failover. At most one node is leader at a time; a node becomes leader only when there is no current leader and it is alive. Only the current leader may admit a car, and it may do so only while the number of cars on the belt is below the belt capacity, which increments the belt count. Cars already on the belt eventually exit, decrementing the count. A control node may crash silently: it drops out of the alive set, and if it was the leader the leadership is cleared so a new leader can be elected by the surviving nodes. A crashed node may later be recovered and rejoin the alive set. Because a car is admitted only while the belt is strictly below capacity, the number of cars on the belt never exceeds the belt capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars on the conveyor belt never exceeds the belt capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m8p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Symbols, MaxCap

VARIABLES lockPhase, finalized, printCount, capacity
vars == <<lockPhase, finalized, printCount, capacity>>

Init ==
  /\ lockPhase = "free"
  /\ finalized = {}
  /\ printCount = 0
  /\ capacity = 1

AcquireCoarse ==
  /\ lockPhase = "free"
  /\ lockPhase' = "coarse"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, printCount, capacity>>

AcquireFine ==
  /\ lockPhase = "coarse"
  /\ lockPhase' = "both"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, printCount, capacity>>

Finalize(sym) ==
  /\ lockPhase = "both"
  /\ sym \notin finalized
  /\ Cardinality(finalized) < capacity
  /\ finalized' = finalized \cup {sym}
  /\ printCount' = printCount + 1
  /\ lockPhase' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

ReleaseFine ==
  /\ lockPhase = "both"
  /\ lockPhase' = "coarse"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, printCount, capacity>>

ReleaseCoarse ==
  /\ lockPhase = "coarse"
  /\ lockPhase' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, printCount, capacity>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ \E k \in 1..MaxCap : k >= Cardinality(finalized) /\ capacity' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lockPhase, finalized, printCount>>

Next ==
  \/ AcquireCoarse \/ AcquireFine \/ ReleaseFine \/ ReleaseCoarse \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E sym \in Symbols : Finalize(sym)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOncePrint == printCount = Cardinality(finalized)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Symbols = {sy1, sy2}
  MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOncePrint
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction finalizes the opening print for each symbol, an irreversible action that may happen at most once per symbol. The engine writes prints under hierarchical locking: it first acquires the coarse session lock, then the fine print lock, and only while holding both may it finalize. Finalizing a symbol records the symbol as finalized, increments a running counter of prints, and releases both locks. A symbol can be finalized only if it has not already been finalized and the number of finalized symbols is still below the session's current capacity. The session capacity can be changed at runtime by an operator, who may raise or lower it, but never below the number of symbols already finalized. The engine may also release the fine and then coarse lock without finalizing. Because the running print counter is advanced exactly once for each symbol added to the finalized set, and a symbol cannot be finalized twice, the print counter always equals the number of finalized symbols.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The running print counter always equals the number of symbols recorded as finalized, so each symbol's opening print happens at most once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m7p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Banks, Slots

None == "none"
AdminId == "admin"

VARIABLES reg, slotOwner, granted
vars == <<reg, slotOwner, granted>>

OwnedCount == Cardinality({s \in Slots : slotOwner[s] # None})

Init ==
  /\ reg = None
  /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> None]
  /\ granted = 0

Acquire(b) ==
  /\ reg = None
  /\ reg' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, granted>>

Allocate(b, s) ==
  /\ reg = b
  /\ slotOwner[s] = None
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = b]
  /\ granted' = granted + 1
  /\ reg' = None

Release(b) ==
  /\ reg = b
  /\ reg' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, granted>>

AdminSeize ==
  /\ reg # AdminId
  /\ reg' = AdminId
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, granted>>

AdminAllocate(s) ==
  /\ reg = AdminId
  /\ slotOwner[s] = None
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = AdminId]
  /\ granted' = granted + 1
  /\ reg' = None

AdminRelease ==
  /\ reg = AdminId
  /\ reg' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, granted>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Acquire(b) \/ Release(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks, s \in Slots : Allocate(b, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminAllocate(s)
  \/ AdminSeize \/ AdminRelease

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation == granted = OwnedCount
====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch assigns settlement slots to member banks, serialized by a single compare-and-swap control register. The register is either free, held by a member bank, or held by the admin. A bank claims the register by a compare-and-swap that succeeds only when it is free, becoming the holder; while holding it, the bank allocates a currently unowned slot to itself, writing itself as the slot's owner, incrementing a running counter of granted allocations, and releasing the register. A bank holding the register with nothing to do simply releases it. There is a privileged admin override: the settlement administrator may seize the register directly at any time regardless of who holds it, and while holding it may allocate an unowned slot to the admin, likewise incrementing the granted counter and releasing the register; the admin may also release without allocating. Because a slot can be allocated only while it is unowned, each slot goes from unowned to owned exactly once, so the running count of granted allocations always equals the number of slots that currently have an owner.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The running count of granted allocations always equals the number of settlement slots that currently have an owner, so no slot is ever allocated twice.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m6p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Aircraft, Total

VARIABLES free, leased, reqd
vars == <<free, leased, reqd>>

Init ==
  /\ free = Total
  /\ leased = 0
  /\ reqd = {}

Request(a) ==
  /\ a \notin reqd
  /\ reqd' = reqd \cup {a}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<free, leased>>

Grant(a) ==
  /\ a \in reqd
  /\ free > 0
  /\ free' = free - 1
  /\ leased' = leased + 1
  /\ reqd' = reqd \ {a}

Expire ==
  /\ leased > 0
  /\ leased' = leased - 1
  /\ free' = free + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED reqd

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Request(a) \/ Grant(a)
  \/ Expire

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SlotsConserved == free + leased = Total
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Aircraft = {ac1, ac2}
  Total = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SlotsConserved
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a fixed number of runway slots, each of which is at any moment either in the free pool or held under a time-limited lease by an aircraft. The total number of slots is fixed and slots are never created or destroyed. Aircraft submit lease requests over a link that may reorder them, so pending requests sit in an unordered set and may be granted in any order. The allocator grants a lease by moving one slot from the free pool into the leased set, but only while the free pool is non-empty, and consuming the matching request. Leases are time-limited: rather than being released by the holder, a lease expires when its term elapses, at which point the allocator automatically returns that slot from the leased set back to the free pool. Because every grant and every expiry only relocates one slot between the free pool and the leased set without adding or removing any, the number of free slots plus the number of leased slots always equals the fixed total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free runway slots plus the number of leased runway slots always equals the fixed total number of slots.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m8p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cranes, Stacks

None == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, stackLock, pos
vars == <<coarse, stackLock, pos>>

Init ==
  /\ coarse = None
  /\ stackLock = [s \in Stacks |-> None]
  /\ pos = [c \in Cranes |-> None]

AcquireYard(c) ==
  /\ coarse = None
  /\ coarse' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stackLock, pos>>

AcquireStack(c, s) ==
  /\ coarse = c
  /\ stackLock[s] = None
  /\ stackLock' = [stackLock EXCEPT ![s] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, pos>>

Enter(c, s) ==
  /\ coarse = c
  /\ stackLock[s] = c
  /\ pos[c] = None
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![c] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, stackLock>>

Leave(c) ==
  /\ pos[c] # None
  /\ stackLock' = [stackLock EXCEPT ![pos[c]] = None]
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![c] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED coarse

ReleaseYard(c) ==
  /\ coarse = c
  /\ \A s \in Stacks : stackLock[s] # c
  /\ coarse' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stackLock, pos>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : AcquireYard(c) \/ Leave(c) \/ ReleaseYard(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Stacks : AcquireStack(c, s) \/ Enter(c, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualExclusion ==
  /\ \A c \in Cranes : pos[c] # None => stackLock[pos[c]] = c
  /\ \A s \in Stacks : stackLock[s] # None => coarse = stackLock[s]
====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is operated by two independent controller instances whose cranes share one common pool of container stacks. Each stack is a critical resource that at most one crane may work in at a time. Access uses hierarchical locking: a crane must first acquire the coarse yard lock, then a stack's fine lock, and only a crane holding the coarse lock may take a stack lock. Only a crane that holds a stack's fine lock may enter that stack to work in it. When a crane leaves a stack it releases the stack's fine lock. A crane releases the coarse yard lock only once it holds no stack locks. Because the coarse yard lock is held by at most one crane at a time and a stack can be fine-locked only by the coarse-lock holder, whenever a crane is inside a stack that stack's fine lock names exactly that crane, and any held stack lock is held by the current coarse-lock holder. Cranes from both controller instances contend for the same yard lock and the same shared stacks, so the guarantee holds across both instances.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a crane is working inside a stack, that stack's fine lock names exactly that crane, so no two cranes ever work in the same stack at once.
